newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sappi jumps as paper, pulp cycle seen on up.
newsitem.headline: Sappi jumps as paper, pulp cycle seen on up.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Sappi Ltd leapt to a five month high on Wednesday on perceptions that the volatile paper and pulp cycle had touched bottom, analysts and dealers said.
Sappi, which on Monday slid as low as 39 rand on a steep slide in half year earnings, notched up 270 cents or 6.5 percent to a high of 44.30 rand in brisk dealings.
"Pulp prices are starting to increase. The cycle looks to have bottomed," said Nico Lambrechts, an analyst at brokerage Huysamer Stals.
He said, although earnings for the full year to end September would remain below last year's, a massive recovery was anticipated in 1998.
"Earnings (per share) for the full 1997 year should be around 209 cents from 230 cents in 1996. But in 1998 I expect a 300 percent increase to 884 cents," he said.

Interim results released at the start of the week showed earnings per share tumbling to just 16 cents from 215 cents at the halfway stage a year ago as low product prices bit a huge chunk out of Sappi's bottom line.

But the firm said that most major suppliers had announced price increases in recent months that would be effective from May and -- unlike attempts to push through hikes earlier in the year -- these rises were being accepted by the market.
It also said the key North American market looked as if it would be riding the crest of the long-awaited upturn in the cycle.
Stock exchange dealers said Sappi's climb on Wednesday was helped by arbitrage trade where investors develop an appetite for big index stocks.
Further upside was seen for the share.
"It could track up to 75 or 80 rand. That's about fair value," Lambrechts said.
By 1045 GMT Sappi had edged off its highs to 43.90 cents, a gain of 230 cents.
